Dental implants are a modern solution for missing teeth. They are based upon small titanium bodies with artificial high-tech tooth roots that become a part of the jaw. They provide a stable base for single-tooth crowns, larger bridges or dentures.

Implants have a completely natural tooth feel, they alleviate the problems of loose or embarrassing dentures and do not necessitate damaging adjacent teeth to fix bridges. Adequate healthy bone must be available to support an implant and the oral environment should be free of any uncontrolled disease.
If insufficient bone is available, predictable techniques for bone augmentation are available.

The implant is placed atraumatically into the jaw using local anaesthetic. A healing period of around 8 weeks follows, while the bony attachment matures. Impressions are then taken for fabrication of the tooth, bridge or denture.
The surgery is pain free, but slight swelling or soreness will be experienced for one to two days after implant placement.

Oliver works very closely with a highly skilled and experienced dental technician who employs the latest techniques and technology in the production of the teeth supported by your implants. We will often arrange an individual consultation with our technician to customise your dental solution. Only the highest quality implants and components are used.

Whether you are referred by your own dentist or simply decide yourself that you would like to know more about how dental implants could benefit you, the first step is to arrange your initial consultation. Call us on 01865 515755 or email us info@oakthorpedental.co.uk to book your appointment with Oliver Brown

Oliver will carefully listen to your concerns and wishes, thoroughly appraise your dental health and explain to you in a clear and concise manner whether or not dental implant treatment would work for you. This first meeting is intended to be a fact finding session, so that you can gather as much information as you need to make an informed choice. Oliver will also outline the procedure for dental implants, the time frames and relevant costs for treatment.

Before a final decision is made about the type of treatment most suitable for you, it is often necessary to gather more precise information in the form of radiographs (xrays), photographs, models and occasionally CT scans. None of this would be undertaken without you having a clear understanding of the costs involved. The planning stage of dental implant treatments is the most important stage. Thorough gathering of relevant information and meticulous planning ensures smooth treatment progression and a predictable outcome.

Once all the necessary information has been gathered and assessed, Oliver will discuss the various treatment solutions relevant to your dental situation. Together you will be able to compare the merits and costs of a dental implant treatment. This will be followed by a written treatment plan.

Oliver believes that from the outset, it is essential that you are fully informed of the cost of your treatment. He will provide a clear, written, fixed quotation for your completed dental implant treatment.

When all information has been gathered and a definitive treatment plan agreed, the treatment appointments will be booked. Oliver will explain what you can expect at each stage of treatment and the time frames between stages. The team at Oakthorpe Dental will do everything they can to ensure that your treatment progresses in a calm and predictable fashion.

The care of your dental implant solution is paramount in ensuring a long term, predictable outcome. Oliver and our team will make sure that you are fully versed in all aspects of caring for your implant treatment.
We welcome specialist implant referrals from other dental practices.

At Oakthorpe Dental we strongly believe in a preventative approach to oral health and we encourage regular hygienist visits. Millions of bacteria are building on your teeth on a daily basis and if left unchecked can lead to problems such as bad breath, bleeding gums, infections and loose teeth.Your gums form the foundation for your teeth and looking after them is paramount to your oral health.

A professional dental hygienist will assess your oral health and form recommendations for further visits, as well as educate you on at-home care. Let the journey to your best smile begin, one dental hygienist appointment at a time

Our team of very experienced hygienists are dedicated to helping you achieve and maintain healthy gums for life. They will thoroughly yet gently clean your teeth and gums in addition to helping you improve your own technique at home.Our aim is to always encourage and motivate you!

Our tooth whitening system is a very simple and effective way to brighten your smile. Custom made whitening trays are fabricated to fit your teeth and the professional whitening gel is applied to them.
These are then worn overnight or approximately 3-4 hours a day. Every day you will notice your teeth gradually changing shade, allowing you the time to assess when you are happy with your new smile.
We always offer a complimentary review appointment to ensure you are happy with the results.

Orthodontics is a type of dental treatment that aims to improve the appearance, position and function of crooked or malaligned teeth.

We offer Invisalign at Oakthorpe Dental which are clear braces to help you straighten your teeth in our practice. Some cases may not be suitable for Invisalign and in these cases we would be happy to refer you to a reputable orthodontist in the local area.
Step 1. Call reception to book a consultation on 01865 515755 or E-mail: info@oakthorpedental.co.uk
Step 2. We will arrange a comprehensive consultation for you.
Step 3. We will provide you with a written report including your treatment options and their costs.
Step 4. Once you have decided that your are ready for braces, we will take your records and have your brace ordered.
Step 5. After 4-6 weeks your braces should be ready to be fitted.
At Oakthorpe Dental we will try our best to provide a simple payment plan to allow you to spread the cost of your treatment.

Grinding your teeth at night (also known as bruxism) is very common, and so is clenching your teeth at night. It seems to be a mostly subconcious behaviour, and the cause is not fully understood. It does seem that this often gets worse during periods of stress.

The problem is when signs and symptoms appear. This can include tooth wear, fractures, pain, limited movement of the jaw joint, migraines or headaches. The muscles involved in moving the jaw can also become tender.
This can, in turn, affect the overall quality of your sleep, leading to chronic sleep deprivation.
Not all cases need to be treated, but if you are concerned this may be affecting you, please get in touch with us and we can discuss it further.
Even though there are many ways to manage bruxism/clenching, the most common treatment is an occlusal splint (dental appliances).
Occlusal splints are generally designed to act as a mechanical separation of the teeth and may be as simple as a soft mouthguard.
Generally one is worn over the lower teeth (or upper) and is made out of soft acrylic. Designed to be comfortable in your mouth as you will need to sleep while wearing the appliance.

If you find the acrylic is too soft then we generally move to make splints out of harder acrylic. There is a transitional period while you get used to wearing this, and you will need review appointments to monitor the success of the appliance.
SCi - Sleep Clench Inhibitor is the most clinically effective FDA-approved treatment for TMD, bruxism, and medically diagnosed migraines.

The SCi reduces abnormal or parafunctional intensity of the temporalis muscles, masseters muscles and to a degree, the lateral pterygoids (these are the tiny muscles at your jaw joints that open your jaw). This eliminates posterior and canine teeth contact, which reduces the temporalis muscle from clenching.

Essentially this means that your back teeth and your canines are kept out of contact while you are wearing the appliance. This reduces the muscle activity which is driving the clenching/bruxism. In turn, this reduces signs and symptoms as stated above.
